doc.title: Ran Blake interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 16, 2021

title: Writing music down, ear dyslexia and shocking records
summary: Blake on his Bard sonata, dyslexia, listening to records growing up and a Shostakovich chord in Hartford.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: What about the mechanical part of writing your music down?

I do very little — I did a piano sonata for my graduation at Bard College and Gunther said, “Good, Ran, join mankind. You really are mediocre sometimes.” So, but I just knew compositions that you have the B theme. Then you have improvisation, and then there’s a fancy word when you come back and repeat the themes in different keys.
Ah yes, the recapitulation I think.

Yes recapitulation. And I had to say this on an oral test at Bard College but I — maybe, probably as a kid I had dyslexia on reading, and now I have ear dyslexia. If I’m going to learn a language I can read it but I just had my record player on all the time in Springfield, Massachusetts and wherever, and later New York and here. And so I’ve missed many events of growing up. I just had to hear this record, “Scythian Suite” by Prokofiev, Shostakovich’s Tenth Symphony. I remember standing up at the Bushnell Memorial Auditorium in Hartford when one chord was — Shostakovich is sometimes a milder composer but there’s a shocking chord in the first movement and I screamed out © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

loud, and some guy behind me said, “Should I put some restraint on you?” But, and then Monk, how he ended “I Should Care.” Chris Connor’s version of “Driftwood” which nobody seems to play anymore. Abbey’s “Throw It Away,” “Down Here Below”, Mal Waldron “Straight Ahead.”

That’s certainly something for those moments. I had one where I was at a Mahavishnu Orchestra concert with John McLaughlin and Billy Cobham did something on the drums that made me like leap out of my seat. And I’m not prone to do that kind of thing.
